I couldn't sleep last night.  I can't sleep on my plane to DC.  Too much sadness, anger, and fear.  

I’m not supposed to be in Congress.  Seven months ago, I got elected to the Florida Senate.  I worked hard to get there.   I was excited thinking I'd have a four year break before another election.  

I couldn’t have imagined that two weeks later, I’d get called to run for Congress.  It wasn’t part of my plan.  It wasn't part of my family's.  

But G-d puts us where He wants us to be.   And as I sit on my flight to DC this morning, struggling to comprehend that I live in a country where Jews can be burned because they are Jews, I know at least one reason He put me here.  

80 years ago they burned us too.  Call your Jewish friends today.  They will tell you that it feels like we are being hunted.  That it is open season.  We are experiencing anti-Semitic hate unlike anything we have ever experienced. 

But there is hope. 

Florida is the safest place in America to be Jewish, and that is not by coincidence.   Together with my friends in the House and Senate -- and they are more than colleagues to me -- we passed bill after bill, most that I initially wrote by hand.  

It came at a cost.  Two people made death threats against my family that landed them in prison.  

It hasn't gone perfectly.  There are still issues.  And some could have done more.   But there has been massive progress. 

I am new in Congress, and as the guy who just showed up, I'm as low on the totem pole as you can be. 

But I am going to work with whoever is willing and whoever I have to in order to solve this problem.  And I will fight whoever opposes us, including anyone on my side who gets in my way.   

I did not come up with my nickname, but it does suit me. 

My power has always been my voice, and I won't be afraid to use it. 

Those who try to shout me down -- like the lunatics who comment here — the leftists, the Nazis, the Muslim terrorists, the woke right, and those who I beat along the way — every comment gives me more strength and more purpose. 

It refires the forge that was lit when I was a 13 year old boy facing my own trials of antisemitism. 

So keep it coming.   You just make me more determined.  You fuel the forge. 

My plane is getting ready to land in DC.  The battle is right in front of me. 

I am ready to fight.  I know we will win.  

Because we have a secret weapon:

We have G-d on our side.

#BombsAway

Blocking a road is a form of terror.   It stops medical emergencies.  It keeps people from living their lives. 

In Florida, I helped pass a bill to allow you to run them over.

Now I'm taking it national. 

The Thump Thump Act is coming.  

Drive away. 

 https://t.co/SDiMNhqk45

Recess-palooza stop #7-- visited @AdventHealth's hospital in Daytona Beach to see cutting-edge health care technologies that can improve outcomes and lower cost!   As former Chairman of the @myflhouse Health Committee, we made tons of improvements in this area!  @AdventHealthCFL https://t.co/hl50lK1QdO

This is how I feel every day, from the time I wake up until the time I go to sleep.  

It's how I've felt every day since October 7th.  

I am so grateful to have a President with the moral clarity to see evil for what it is. 

G-d blessed us with Donald Trump.   May both of them save the tortured souls who have suffered so much.

Recess-palooza stop #13 -- according to the 41 year-tenured Director, I was the first Congressman to ever take a tour of @palmcoastgov Wastewater Treatment Plant #1, which will be undergoing a several hundred million dollar expansion.   

I've worked on Florida water issues since I was first elected to the Florida House, and am excited to keep doing it in Congress. 

Thanks to Vice Mayor Theresa Pontieri and Councilmen Ty Miller and David Sullivan for showing me around and to @FlaglerLive @NewsFlagler @PalmCoastNowFL @BuzzFlagle438 @AskFlagler and @dbnewsjournal for joining us.

Recess-palooza stop #14 -- Great to meet with Bunnell Mayor Catherine Robinson and City Manager Alvin Jackson to let them know I have secured $5.16 million for their Wastewater Treatment project!   While some local politicians just grandstand, working with my office, these guys got the job done.

Recess-palooza event #18 -- Two days, two beaches!  (Though not in a bathing suit).   Today, I toured the beaches of @CountyOfVolusia with the County team.  Excited to see a strategy to try to return to natural dune coverage as a way to protect the beach.  I’ll be working with them to help them take this to the next level!

I was honored to secure funding for the Bunnell Wastewater Treatment Facility Modernization Project. Providing my district with the infrastructure needed to deliver clean water to all of my wonderful constituents is a necessity. Huge win for FL-06! https://t.co/gg0oi7YerH

Back Home Stop #21: excited to speak to the @DaytonaChamber at the  @BBraunUSA medical manufacturing facility, sponsored by @NASCAR!  Great town hall with this bipartisan group! https://t.co/keLeVPVw8x

Recess Stop 37: I got to meet with our Belleview district office landlord and Mayor, Christine Dobkowski. 

Serving since 2011, Mayor Dobkowski has accomplished a lot, from supporting small businesses to securing $9.9 million in funding for wastewater treatment expansion. 

Mayor Dobkowski continues to secure big wins, and it was a pleasure to chat with her!

At Home Stop #47: I met with State Rep. Nan Cobb and her team to discuss how we can work with the White House on keeping Lake County safe and ensure we are working together to improve mental health services in Central Florida. https://t.co/40GgsRodkI
